Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-07-20 | AMZN | Overweight | -7.4% | -7.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AMZN, but earned in stages rather than chased at spot. Start with a quarter-size probe near 249.99 carrying only 0.25–0.5% of book risk (not the full 1% half-size starter), with the structural stop at 241.70 (~1.1x ATR); add on a stabilized retest of 243–247 that reclaims 247.07 without a negative MACD histogram cross to reach ~1.0x standard, and only push to a maximum ~1.25x after the 10-Q validates the demand backlog. Do not add into the 256.65–258.08 rejection zone, keep pre-earnings size at or below ~0.5x standard given the 5–10% gap history (6/26, 2/6, 4/30), and earn full size only on a daily close above 252.89 on volume ≥45M. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The franchise case wins the rating; the entry-timing objections win the sizing. That split, not a tie, is what produces Overweight rather than Buy or Hold.

What decided the direction. The hardest datapoint in this debate is uncontested and conceded by the conservative analyst: AMZN expanded operating margin ~131bp to a record 13.1% and grew operating income +29.6% to $23.85B *while* absorbing a +32.8% surge in depreciation — real operating leverage during the heaviest phase of the capex buildout. Add revenue +16.6% to $181.5B, a record 51.8% gross margin, and TTM operating cash flow of $148.5B (+30%), and the earnings engine is genuinely compoundable. The aggressive analyst's rerated core EPS of ~$1.92 (+21% YoY) after stripping the $12.3B non-cash mark survives scrutiny because the conservative analyst accepted the recalculation. Solvency is not the issue either: D/E ~0.31x, current ratio 1.18x, ~$144B liquidity roughly matching ~$138.8B gross debt, and >25x interest coverage on operating income. Demand visibility — $20.9B deferred revenue and $569B of contractual obligations — was called "unverified" but never rebutted.

What the bears won, and why it controls execution. The entry at 249.99 is mid-range and under resistance. AMZN sits below a falling 50-SMA at 251.63 and has closed above it once in 28 sessions (7/15, given back the next day); the 7/20 push to 252.89 was rejected on only 32.4M shares against roughly a 49M average; 256.65–258.08 has rejected twice, including 7/16 closing near the session low on 45.34M shares — that is supply, not a lagging-average artifact. The MACD histogram has contracted four sessions (2.124 → 1.446) with the line still above zero, RSI 54, and price only ~1.8% above VWMA 245.58. The conservative analyst is also right that a 241.70 stop is not a guarantee into an earnings print with a demonstrated 5–10% gap history, and that the quality of earnings is not clean: TTM FCF ~−$2.5B against ~$151B TTM capex, $53.4B of long-term debt issued in a single quarter, interest expense +48% YoY, $48.1B of illiquid non-marketable-equity marks that can reverse symmetrically, and an effective tax rate stepping from 21.0% to 24.0%.

Where I side against each extreme. Against the aggressive analyst: calling the downside "structurally capped" at 241.70 and treating the coil as already resolved higher is overreach, and the Trainium "$20B run-rate" and Anthropic "$1.2T IPO" items are syndicated narrative with no disclosed revenue basis, stake size, or timeline — optionality that justifies holding through volatility, not upsizing ahead of an event. Against the conservative analyst: "no new buy at 249.99" gives up too much. Four of the last five AMZN calls here were cautious (Underweight x3, Hold x2) and every one produced positive five-day alpha *against* the stance, with each reflection landing on the same diagnosis — a name above a rising 200-SMA (234.21) with a clean higher-low sequence (225.55 → 240.52 → 243.59), rising VWMA, and MACD above zero was discounted on entry mechanics, not on thesis. The GOOGL/AAPL lesson (trimming into a sub-1-ATR resistance level in confirmed momentum was the losing half) and the 2026-07-06 lesson (an entry-timing discount, not the thesis, was the marginal variable) both say to seed a starter rather than stand aside. The neutral analyst's conditional-buy middle path — quarter-size now at 0.25–0.5% book risk, or wait for the 243–247 retest that reclaims 247.07, or the 252.89/45M-share breakout — is the correct calibration, and I adopt it, with the one adjustment that a caller already long AMZN should not add here and should trim or hedge into the event window.

What would change the call. Upgrade to Buy and max size on a daily close above 252.89 on volume ≥45M plus a Q2 print showing revenue holding ≥15%, operating income growth ≥25% ex the non-operating mark, and no capex raise without a matching revenue raise. Downgrade toward Underweight on a daily close below 247.07 with a negative MACD histogram cross (opens 242.34, then 234.21), and cut to minimal on a daily close below the rising 200-SMA at 234.21. A capex raise without a revenue raise is the highest-probability negative catalyst and should be treated as a trim signal, and a headline EPS miss driven by a mark reversal must be reconciled to core EPS before it moves a share of size.

Explicit evidence gaps, not priced in either direction: insider-transaction data is DATA_UNAVAILABLE; the $569B obligation figure is unresolvable line-by-line without the 10-Q footnotes, so it informs sizing, not valuation; no segment-level AWS/advertising revenue or ROIC is provided; no portfolio or holdings context was supplied, so all sizing is stated as fractions of a standard AMZN allocation.

**Price Target**: 264.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -7.0% (raw -7.4%) says the Overweight call was wrong in the immediate window, though five days is too short to judge a 3–6 month franchise thesis. It supports the bears’ execution objection—buying mid-range at 249.99 below the falling 50-SMA and into the 256.65–258.08 supply zone—and undercuts the staged-probe sizing, while the margin/backlog thesis was not tested. Next time, with price below a falling 50-SMA, repeated rejection, and earnings-gap risk, do not seed a starter before a 252.89 close on ≥45M shares or a 243–247 retest that reclaims 247.07; make the event/breakout the trigger, not the valuation.

[2026-07-17 | AMZN | Hold | -6.1% | -5.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Maintain the AMZN core position at standard benchmark allocation and put no new capital to work at $247.23. The setup is genuinely two-sided — a rising 200 SMA at $234.06 and intact golden cross versus a failed breakout below a declining 50 SMA at $252.13 — so this is a trigger-driven hold, not a chase and not a trim. Add only on a daily close above $252.5 on above-average volume with an expanding MACD histogram (first 25% tranche, second 25% only above $258), or on a two-session stabilization in $234–237 that holds the VWMA/200 SMA (up to 50%). Hard cap at 1.0x standard until FCF inflects or $258 confirms; close-based invalidation: below $240 cut to 50% of standard, below $228 with golden-cross breakdown go to minimum exposure. Horizon 3–6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: The three risk seats converge on Hold but split on whether to pre-position, and weighed independently the business-quality and next-quarter evidence genuinely cancel. The aggressive seat wins the franchise argument, which the other two concede: Q1 revenue +16.6% to $181.5B, operating income +29.6% to $23.85B, margin +130 bps to 13.1%, TTM OCF $148.5B (+28%), ~$144B cash/securities, price 5.6% above a rising 200 SMA at $234.06 with the golden cross intact, and margins expanding while depreciation rose ~33% — a direct answer to the depreciation-cliff concern.

But the conservative seat wins the accounting, cash-flow and tape dimensions, and those points stand unanswered: (1) 'net-cash neutral' only survives by excluding ~$91.6B of operating leases — total debt roughly doubled to ~$122B on $53.4B of new long-term paper, interest expense +48% YoY, $569.3B of contractual obligations; not fatal against $148.5B OCF but the 'fortress' framing is overstated. (2) TTM capex $151.0B now exceeds TTM OCF $148.5B, Q1 burned -$18.2B of FCF, and capitalized-but-unpaid capex is still rising — 'FCF inflects when capex plateaus' is a forecast with no visible plateau. (3) The $225B Trainium figure is a CEO-sourced headline with no 10-Q footnote, definition, timing or cancellation terms; the aggressive attempt to reframe capex as contracted backlog cannot carry the weight, and the neutral seat is right that it is not an add signal. The $12.3B PE markup (30-40% of the $2.78 diluted EPS) is reversible, non-operating earnings that overstate run-rate.

The tape tiebreaker favors the defensive read on specifics: two rejections at $255.95-$258.08 (7/16 intraday 258.08, closed back inside at 249.89), a red 7/17 close at $247.23 on above-average 43.6M volume, price below a declining 50 SMA, golden-cross spread compressing from 24.3 to 18.1 points, and price only ~1% above the VWMA at $244.79 — lose that line and the volume read flips to distribution. The 'coiled spring' framing requires ignoring a failed breakout on the day the best stock-specific news hit; and a starter into $242-245 with a $239.5 stop is undisciplined when ATR is 7.59 (~3.1%), since that stop is inside normal noise and $242-245 is the exact shelf that failed on 7/17.

On sizing I side with the neutral seat: the conservative 1.0x cap is right until FCF stabilizes (1.25x only after a confirmed $258 close and non-deteriorating FCF/leverage), and the range is honored as having a fatter left tail than the chart implies by requiring confirmation. Risk/reward from $247 is roughly symmetric (-5.6% to the 200 SMA, -7.7% to the $228.16 lower band, -8.8% to the June $225.55 low versus ~+7% to $265), and the largest bullish pillar is unverifiable from disclosure, so I will not manufacture a direction out of a balanced setup.

What changes the call: upgrade toward Overweight on a daily close above $252.5 on above-average volume with an expanding MACD histogram, second tranche above $258, backed by Q2 evidence of capex deceleration and a narrowing OCF-vs-capex gap. Downgrade toward Underweight on a daily close below $240 with continued negative FCF and rising leverage, or below $228 with golden-cross breakdown. Evidence gaps not underwritten: definition/timing/counterparty/cancellation terms of the $225B commitments (needs the 10-Q purchase-obligation footnote or call transcript), whether capitalized-but-unpaid capex and the $151B capex line are still climbing, Amazon's own advertising growth rate, effective tax normalization as deferred taxes unwind, and mark-to-model assumptions on the $12.3B PE markup. No segment-level ROIC or AWS margin split and only a partial news sample were provided.

**Price Target**: 254.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of -5.5% (raw -6.1%, price down to roughly $232 from $247.23) shows the near-term direction was down and that the Hold was too passive, though five sessions cannot judge a 3–6 month thesis. It validates the conservative seat's tape read — the failed breakout at $255.95–258.08, the declining 50 SMA, and the "fatter left tail than the chart implies" — and it triggered the stated $240 close-based invalidation within days, meaning the framing was correct but the sizing rule never got to act. The aggressive seat's franchise and margin evidence was simply not tested by this window. Lesson for next time: when the bearish tape tiebreaker wins and the invalidation level sits within one ATR (~3.1%) of spot, act on it with a pre-emptive trim rather than parking at full Hold and waiting for a close to confirm.
